newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond issues quiet but more seen soon.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond issues quiet but more seen soon.

text.p: As corporate bond new issue activity winds down for the week, players still wait with anticipation for any surprise issuance that may pop into the market, dealers said.
"The market still has a good tone to it...I imagine we could still see some surprise issuance today," said one syndicate source.
Despite the absence of a forward calendar, dealers said with U.S. Treasury yields at such attractive levels issuers may be prompted to come to market now, rather than later.
"The tone in the (new issue) market is very good and should continue to move along at a pretty good clip as rates keep getting more and more attractive," another syndicate source said.
As supply continues to be met with good demand, dealers said they expect issues to keep flowing at a steady pace.
"The demand for paper has been there so the pace for debt issuance is likely to contine," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Going forward, dealers expect issuance to pick up ahead of the upcoming November U.S. Presidential election and while rates are still low.
"I think activity will pick up even more ahead of the elections while rates are at such low levels," another syndicate source said.
Meanwhile, Goodyear is set to issue $100 million in 10-year debt via Goldman Sachs & Co, dealers said.
International Home Foods Inc is expected to price $400 million in senior 144A notes due 2006 via Chase Securities, sources said.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds are up 9/32 at 99-20/32 to yield 6.78 percent.
